comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
INVESTIGATION (why code-review findings score disproportionately low): root cause is that impact() measures PRODUCTION-INCIDENT severity, which is the wrong yardstick for a maintainability gate. impact = mean(max(prod_impact,debt_impact), blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility), scale floored at 0.33.

Evidence — attribute distributions, SAME model:
- PLAN-REVIEW would-block (n=921): prod_impact high=59%, blast module+=98%, likelihood high=78%, reversibility moderate/hard=84% => impact 0.78+.
- CODE-REVIEW (n=31): prod_impact none/low=96% (0% high), reversibility easy=93%, blast local/module, debt_impact never high => impact structurally capped ~0.25-0.60.

So plan-review findings are production-CONSEQUENCE-shaped (the model fits); code-review findings are MAINTENANCE/DETECTION-GAP-shaped (the model has no axis for them). Concrete perversities:
1. A silently-dead feature (untested wiring #10) is rated prod_impact=NONE — the model asks 'does it crash now', not 'does it fail to work / go undetected'.
2. reversibility INVERTS the signal: 'easy to reverse' lowers impact, but a missing test being easy-to-add-later is exactly why it's a latent landmine; the model rewards the wrong thing. 93% of code-review findings are 'easy' => everything pinned near the 0.33 floor on that axis.
3. debt_impact (the one axis meant for tech-debt) is capped — verifier never emits 'high', and it only counts via max(prod,debt).

Implication: code-review priority-blocking is not tunable by threshold (landmines & nits both compressed into 0.4-0.6, overlapping). Fixes: (a) a maintainability-appropriate impact model for the code_review gate — debt-primary, add a detection-gap/latent-regression axis, drop or invert reversibility for detection findings; and/or (b) block on a semantic CLASS (DET new-behavior-without-test) that sidesteps the broken scalar. This deepens the original idea: it's not just 'the mean dilutes' — the AXES are wrong for this gate + reversibility is inverted for detection findings.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: EXPERIMENT: Sonnet-scored sim on 48 labeled plan-review findings (38 VALID / 10 BORDERLINE, both high-severity). RESULT: VALID vs BORDERLINE is NOT impact-separable (every model incl. old ~AUC 0.50; best single sub-q S3-decomposition 0.60; some axes anti-correlate). => the residual VALID/BORDERLINE boundary is altitude/already-handled/urgency, NOT impact magnitude, so an impact-model rework adds little SEPARATION there. Sub-question reliability was ~1.0 (decomposition works). The one evidence-consistent, research-backed change that directly fixes the ORIGINAL band-stranding complaint: replace the diluting MEAN with SEVERITY-FIRST MAX + hard override (FMEA Action-Priority) so a single high axis isn't averaged below the bar — no new axes needed. Optionally add the detection amplifier (silent-vs-self-revealing was reliable, AUC-neutral here) and wire the now-deterministic decomposition signal (G5 fix). NOTE: plan-impact rework is LOWER priority than the already-decided 0.60 threshold-lowering + G5 determinism, which capture the stranded findings directly.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
During review-threshold re-tuning (2026-07) we found that genuinely high-severity plan-review AND code-review findings systematically score priority 0.60-0.69 and fall just under the 0.70 block bar. Root cause: `priority = validity x impact`, and `impact` is the unweighted MEAN of 5 severity attributes (prod_impact, debt_impact, blast_radius, likelihood, reversibility). A finding that is critical on one axis but 'easy'/'local' on others gets averaged down (e.g. critical prod-impact + easy reversibility + module blast -> impact ~= 0.67), so real blocks land below the bar and ship as advisory.

We worked around it by lowering per-criterion block_thresholds to 0.60, but the aggregation itself is the deeper lever.

## Why revisit
- Threshold-lowering is a blunt fix; it also admits any finding that happens to average ~0.60.
- The mean conflates 'severe on the dimension that matters' with 'mild overall'. A max, weighted, or severity-gated aggregation (e.g. a critical prod_impact should floor impact regardless of reversibility) would let high-severity findings clear the bar on merit without lowering thresholds globally.
- Same mechanism affects code-review (findings cap ~0.67).

## Possible directions (to design later)
- Weighted aggregation (prod_impact / blast_radius weighted higher than reversibility).
- max-of-attributes or a severity-gated floor for critical/major.
- Decouple 'is it block-worthy' from 'validity x mean-impact' entirely (a learned/ruled block-worthiness signal).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Not scheduled — parking-lot idea. Revisit after the 0.60 threshold change has run in production and we can measure block-rate/precision under it.
compiled_state.title: Rework review impact aggregation — mean-of-5-attributes dilutes high-severity findings below the block bar
